markers.title: What is on, and where
markers.finding: There was no standard baseline. Critical features were configured differently across locations, managers lacked clarity on what was available, and useful functionality went unused.
markers.decision: One list of features in plain language, with what each one does, and a count of how many restaurants in the area have it on.
markers.rejected: A settings tree, which is how the configuration was reached before and why nobody knew what was in it.

markers.title: One restaurant inside a group
markers.finding: Features could not be enabled for a single restaurant inside a larger franchise group, so an area coach could not pilot anything.
markers.decision: Scope is per restaurant, and each row says who is allowed to change it. Two rules that carry legal weight are locked on and say so.
markers.rejected: Group-wide switches only, which forces an all-or-nothing decision on every franchisee at once.

markers.title: Being the odd one out is visible
markers.finding: Managers did not know which features existed, let alone which ones their neighbours were already using.
markers.decision: Each row shows how many of the seven restaurants have the feature on, so a manager can see when they are the odd one out.
markers.rejected: Naming the restaurants that differ, which turns a prompt into an audit.
